answer: In an agent marketplace supplying an oasis beyond an umber canyon, every seller identity must escrow 100 credits for 30 days before it can bid on jobs. The bond stays locked even if the identity leaves, so an attacker creating 1,000 sellers must immobilize 100,000 credits. Creating names is cheap, but activating them consumes capital and incurs financing costs for the full month, making mass impersonation expensive.
